text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batcher latency spike + node flaps detected in us-west-2. Auto-ingest: 1780 errors in 5m, several kube restarts. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/continuous-batcher

Sasha: taking oncall. looking at dashboards now. any customer-facing errors?

Praveen: seeing high 99p for text-gen routes (from ~300ms -> ~12s). Some requests stuck in QUEUED state, not executing. Customer reports of 504s starting ~02:07 UTC.

Maria: checking node metrics — three gpu-nodes rebooted in last 8m. kubelet shows OOM kills for process "redwood-runtime" on those nodes. dmesg on node-3 has repeated lines: `Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (redwood-runtime) total-vm: 1023456kB`

Tim: on the GPU side, driver logs show a few `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and `CUDA_ERROR_OOM` around the same times. attaching a short tail:
```
Mar 02 02:06:42 node-3 redwood-runtime[12345]: kernel: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
Mar 02 02:06:45 node-3 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (redwood-runtime)
Mar 02 02:06:47 node-3 kubelet: Pod redwood/continuous-batcher-7d9c restart
```

Sasha: looks like a combo: batch growth -> allocator pressure -> CUDA faults -> container SIGKILL -> node flip. Could be the heartbeat/accumulator loop we've seen in staging before.

Praveen: can we throttle ingestion temporarily? set rate-limit or route traffic to fallback model variant?

Maria: pushing a quick routing change: updated route map to send new requests to model-x-small across host pool (less memory). patch applied. :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: AUTO: routing change applied to /v1/generate (weights: model-x-small=80%, model-x=20%) by Maria at 02:10 UTC.

Tim: in parallel, I'm SSHing into node-3 to capture full logs and dump runtime state. trying to avoid node reboot if possible to preserve coredumps.

Sasha: mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch/prefill on continuous-batcher to reduce KV cache growth, 2) lower max_batch_size to 8, 3) cordon and drain any node with repeated SIGKILLs once we have coredump, 4) failover traffic to smaller model as Maria did. doing 1+2 now.

Praveen: command for disable prefetch in runtime-config: `kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/continuous-batcher PREFETCH_ENABLED=false` — please confirm before apply.

Sasha: applying now. `kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/continuous-batcher PREFETCH_ENABLED=false && kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher`

Tim: applied restart. rolling restarts across 6 pods, staggering 30s between restarts to avoid thundering herd.

Maria: observed queue depth dropping after disable — QUEUED -> RUNNING transitions improving. 99p latency down to ~3.2s within 90s of change. :thumbsup:

Praveen: still seeing two pods restart unexpectedly with OOMs. I'll cordon node-3 and drain to move any remaining workloads away.

Sasha: cordon/drain commands?

Praveen: `kubectl cordon node-3 && kubectl drain node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60`

Tim: note — when draining node-3 one runtime pod produced a coredump (uploaded to /var/crash/4447778888_node-3_core.gz). Saving for postmortem.

Sasha: handing incident to Praveen for next steps and postmortem tracking. I'm going offline for 30m to grab sleep. Handoff checklist: current mitigations applied (prefetch disabled, max_batch_size=8, routing to model-x-small), cordon node-3, coredump collected, customer comms initialized.

Praveen: acknowledging handoff. I'll stay on until resolution. next actions: investigate accumulator metrics, check heartbeat ack latencies, and prepare a small runtime patch to limit accumulator growth.

Maria: customer alert drafted + sent to affected accounts: short blurb, ETA for fix, contact SRE team.

IncidentBot: UPDATE: severity remains P1. Monitoring automation will re-evaluate in 10m.

Tim: quick triage notes — from coredump and heap snapshots, there are many kv-cache entries pinned by early-prefetch requests; accumulator length grew to 4.2M tokens in one worker before OOM. suspect livelock in heartbeat ack path prevented eviction.

Praveen: good catch. temporary code patch idea: add a hard cap on accumulator tokens per-worker and force early-eviction if > 200k tokens. Can we hotpatch?

Sasha: (from offline) if we can toggle a feature-flag to impose cap, do it. otherwise revert to older runtime with stable prefetch behavior.

Praveen: feature-flag toggle applied: `runtime.FEATURE_ACCUMULATOR_CAP=200000` via config-map and rollout restart. applied at 02:27 UTC.

Maria: latency stabilizing. 99p at ~1.1s, error rate down to baseline. customers reporting degraded but usable responses.

Tim: leaving logs and diagnostics in /tmp/incidents/4447778888/ for postmortem. will attach kernel logs, runtime traces, and coredump.

Praveen: closing the active mitigation — keeping incident open for postmortem tracking and follow-up actions: 1) root-cause confirm via kernel and runtime trace, 2) fix heartbeat ACK path to remove livelock, 3) e2e test for accumulator growth and prefetch backpressure, 4) runbook update for similar incidents.

IncidentBot: RESOLUTION: mitigations successful, traffic back to normal. Incident moved to 'investigating' for follow-up.

Sasha: thanks team. filing postmortem ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml for fix. PRs to land: guard in allocator, prefetch backpressure, and runbook updates. :sparkles:

Praveen: I'll own the follow-up. ETA initial RCA doc in 48h.

DeployBot: NOTE: audit entry created for all config changes.

Maria: done for now. will monitor for 2h then transition to watch rotation.

Tim: saved a short log excerpt and the coredump link: s3://redwood-incident-logs/4447778888/node-3-core.gz

Praveen: last check — all green on dashboards. marking as stable. thanks everyone.
